metadata.note: The Coudersport and Port Allegany Railroad (organized 1881 as the Coudersport & Olean, renamed 1882): Port Allegany (PRR connection) - Coudersport - Newfield Junction (Buffalo and Susquehanna) - Ulysses (Fall Brook / NYC), Potter and McKean counties, Pa., about 39 mi. Drawn from research/branches/coudersport_and_port_allegany_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-10-21. Before this layer the map drew no C&PA trackage. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn; both main-line ends are [OPEN] at 1933, the last confirmed year.
metadata.ownership_splits: None. The C&PA ran its own trains from 1882 until it was sold to the Wellsville, Addison and Galeton in 1964, which falls in freight-only years. WIKIST's 'became part of the New York Central system' in 1899 is the Fall Brook's lease, not a C&PA ownership change. The Jersey Shore, Pine Creek & Buffalo (graded 1874-75, ran no trains) gets no feature.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-10-21 (at creation): nothing drawn for freight-only years. Excluded: Coudersport - Roulette and Coudersport - Newfield Junction freight after passenger service ended (proven freight-only by Aug 1951, G52) to 1964; the Wellsville, Addison and Galeton operation 1964-70 (freight only); the 1951 Coudersport - Port Allegany 'express and mail only' service (not passenger, and by road after the 1942 flood). The Sweden Valley spur ('Pine Creek Division') is omitted for want of any passenger evidence, not because it is proven freight-only.
metadata.horsecar_audit: 2026-10-21 (at creation): none - steam from the 1882 opening; nothing trimmed under Rule 5.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-10-21 (at creation): every label follows Rule 6, 'Coudersport and Port Allegany: <terminal> – <terminal>'.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] Port Allegany - Coudersport: passenger service is confirmed only to 1933 (Fowler c). The end lies between 1933 and the flood of July 18 1942, which destroyed the track west of Roulette; any service Coudersport - Roulette after 1942 is unproven and was gone by Aug 1951 (G52). Leads: Potter Enterprise and Port Allegany Reporter-Argus, ICC / Moody's passenger revenue by year, Pietrak's 1972 history of the line.

[OPEN] Coudersport - Newfield Junction: confirmed only to 1933 (Fowler c(tm)); the end lies between 1933 and Aug 1951. Whether a mixed train carried passengers after 1942 is unproven (report block [6], not drawn).

Coudersport - Newfield Junction start: first confirmed 1896 (1896 Official Guide); WIKI says 'by 1895'. Whether Coudersport - Newfield Junction and Newfield Junction - Ulysses opened together is not established.

Newfield Junction - Ulysses end: 1919 rests on Fowler's undefined 'GG' code (road legend 'p: 1919GG'); 1909 is the last year proven by a readable timetable. The line was abandoned in 1924, so the true end lies between 1919 (or 1909) and 1924.

Terminals missing the late letters: Port Allegany is not lettered c (1933) and Ulysses is not lettered p (1919); both are drawn to the full terminal on the strength of the through timetables, as the report recommends.

OMITTED, no confirmed passenger year: the Sweden Valley spur ('CPA: Pine Creek Division', Coudersport - Ladona - Sweden Valley, about 5-6 mi; Fowler section 386 lists the stations with no date letters; builder and date unknown).
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates on every feature.

properties.line: Coudersport and Port Allegany: Port Allegany – Coudersport
properties.speed_source: estimated for a lightly built steam branch line with 2-3 trains each way a day; not computed from a real timetable (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror): every way tagged old_railway_operator=C&PA (31 ways, all name='Coudersport and Port Allegany Railroad', railway=abandoned/dismantled), plus abandoned/historic railway ways and named rail-trails in the corridor (fetch_gap), traced with opstrace.py (own-tagged ways 1x, untagged 1.25x, paths 3x, other named operators 12x); waypoints geocoded with Nominatim and checked by type (Roulette returned the township and Coudersport the borough centroid - both hand-pinned onto the grade; Crowell returned a hiking trail and was not used); Douglas-Peucker 8 m then trim_reversals. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the whole line (41.70,-78.32 to 41.95,-77.72) and holds no railway ways there. No rail-trail is mapped on the alignment. Every C&PA way in OSM is an unreviewed TIGER import ('Old Railroad Grade', tiger:reviewed=no), so the alignment is only as good as the TIGER grade line; it is a separately mapped grade, not the US 6 roadway, and does not ride any other railroad.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 15.8 mi against the documented 16.5 mi (Fowler: Port Allegany 0.0 - Roulette 7.5 - Coudersport 16.5), 96%. 14.9 mi runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=C&PA; 0.1 mi is short connectors between the ends of adjacent mapped pieces. Two APPROXIMATED legs, both straight gap-bridges between mapped C&PA pieces (0.9 mi in all): (1) east of Mina, 0.26 mi (418 m) where the mapped grade breaks; (2) through Coudersport, 0.6 mi from the end of the mapped grade at the west edge of town (41.7657,-78.0244) north to an approximate station point (41.7745,-78.0223) - OSM maps no C&PA track through the town, and the station point is estimated, not surveyed. The Mina - Coudersport way (1.8 mi) carries an OSM fixme 'rough alignment in places'. Waypoints Burtville, Roulette, Knowlton, Mina are within 0.3 km of the line; the line starts at the west end of the mapped grade, 0.5 km from Port Allegany's borough centroid, beside the PRR (ex-WNY&P) station area. The ~0.7 mi shortfall is the unmapped approach into Port Allegany plus the straight bridge through Coudersport. LATER ALIGNMENT: the road was 3 ft gauge 1882-1889 and was standard-gauged in 1889 (BEERS, WIKI); the grade drawn is the one abandoned in 1942/1970, i.e. the standard-gauge alignment. Whether the 1889 conversion realigned any curves is not known.

segments.note: Coudersport & Olean Railroad (organized 1881), renamed Coudersport and Port Allegany 1882; Port Allegany (PRR, ex-WNY&P Buffalo - Emporium connection) - Colemans - Burtville - Roulette - Knowlton - Mina - Olmsted - Coudersport, up the Allegheny River valley. BEERS: 'On September 26, 1882, the first passenger train passed over the road' (WIKI: first train reached Coudersport Sept 7, formal opening Sept 26; WIKIST's 'October 1882' conflicts but is the same year). Steam (Brooks 4-4-0s) from opening, so no Rule 5 trim. 3 ft gauge until 1889 (BEERS: cars ran over the standard-gauge road in July 1889; WIKI: completed June 16 1889). BEERS records 21,924 passengers in 1888. Public timetables of 1901 (CCP01) and 1909 (CCP09) run from Port Allegany with times; in 1909 trains 1 and 2 ran daily Coudersport - Port Allegany, all others weekdays only. [OPEN] 1933 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: Fowler letters 'c' (1933 company timetable) at Colemans, Boyers, Burtville, Card Creek, Roulette, Knowlton, Mina, Olmsted and Coudersport. No source dates when passenger service actually stopped (secondary sources disagree: 'early 1920s' vs 'thrived until 1942'). Hard limits: the flood of July 18 1942 destroyed the track west of Roulette and it was never replaced (WIKI, ABRAILS, FLICKR); by Aug 1951 the Official Guide shows 'Regular Passenger Service Discontinued', freight only Coudersport - Roulette and 'express and mail service only' (by road) Coudersport - Port Allegany, with every station daggered freight-only (G52). Caveat: Fowler does not letter Port Allegany itself 'c' - only Colemans, 1.9 mi out - so 1933 trains running into the PRR station is an inference, not a proof. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued Coudersport - Roulette into the 1960s; the line was abandoned Dec 8 1970. headway_min is an estimate from the 2-3 trains each way a day in the 1901 and 1909 timetables, NOT a counted figure.
sources: Segment-level: BEERS for the 1882 start; Fowler (JF) section 385 letters z (1897) and c (1933) for the confirmed years; CCP01 and CCP09 timetables; WIKI, ABRAILS and FLICKR for the 1942 flood; G52 for freight-only by Aug 1951. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.

Every C&PA way in OSM is an unreviewed TIGER import ('Old Railroad Grade', tiger:reviewed=no), so the alignment is only as good as the TIGER grade line; it is a separately mapped grade, not the US 6 roadway, and does not ride any other railroad.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 16.0 mi against the documented 15.9 mi (Fowler: Coudersport 16.5 - Newfield Junction 32.4; G52 '16 miles'), 101%. 15.8 mi runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=C&PA. One APPROXIMATED leg: 0.2 mi (360 m) straight gap-bridge from the approximate Coudersport station point north to where the mapped grade resumes (41.7778,-78.0219). Waypoints Colesburg, Raymond and Gold are within 0.2 km of the line. Newfield Junction is drawn at the node OSM shares between the C&PA grade and the ex-Buffalo and Susquehanna grade (tagged old_railway_operator=B&O), 41.8680,-77.8207. About 0.9 mi just west of Colesburg follows grade ways that OSM also tags as a farm track and a driveway. LATER ALIGNMENT: none known; the extension was built standard gauge c.1895-96 and the drawn grade is the one abandoned in 1970.

segments.note: Eastern extension, Coudersport - North Coudersport - Frinks - Colesburg - Seven Bridges - Raymond - Gold - Newfield - Newfield Junction (crossing and connection with the Buffalo and Susquehanna Galeton - Wellsville line; Fowler's earlier 'Buffalo & Susquehanna Junction', the 1909 timetable's 'B. & S. Junction'). Built and run by the C&PA itself; no affiliated company is known for it. 1896 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start: Fowler 'Newfield Junction 1896G' (1896 Official Guide). WIKI says the line was extended 'by 1895', so service probably began a year earlier, but that is unproven. [OPEN] 1933 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: Fowler letters 'c' (1933 company timetable) at every station from North Coudersport to Newfield, and 'Newfield Junction ... c(tm)' - the 1933 eastern terminus of service. No source dates when passenger service actually stopped. By Aug 1951 the Official Guide shows 'Regular Passenger Service Discontinued' and freight only Newfield Junction - Coudersport, every station daggered (G52). After the 1942 flood this was the road's only outlet; an undated, unsourced caption (FLICKR) says one train a day ran Coudersport - Newfield Junction to meet the W.A.G., but that describes 1956 or later (the WAG began Jan 1 1956, AMRAILS) and does not mention passengers, so nothing after 1933 is drawn. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued under the C&PA to 1964 and the Wellsville, Addison and Galeton 1964-70; abandoned Dec 8 1970. headway_min is an estimate from the 2-3 trains each way a day in the 1901 and 1909 timetables, NOT a counted figure.

properties.speed_source: estimated for a lightly built steam branch line with 2-3 trains each way a day; not computed from a real timetable (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror): every way tagged old_railway_operator=C&PA (31 ways, all name='Coudersport and Port Allegany Railroad', railway=abandoned/dismantled), plus abandoned/historic railway ways and named rail-trails in the corridor (fetch_gap), traced with opstrace.py (own-tagged ways 1x, untagged 1.25x, paths 3x, other named operators 12x); waypoints geocoded with Nominatim and checked by type (Roulette returned the township and Coudersport the borough centroid - both hand-pinned onto the grade; Crowell returned a hiking trail and was not used); Douglas-Peucker 8 m then trim_reversals. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the whole line (41.70,-78.32 to 41.95,-77.72) and holds no railway ways there. No rail-trail is mapped on the alignment. Every C&PA way in OSM is an unreviewed TIGER import ('Old Railroad Grade', tiger:reviewed=no), so the alignment is only as good as the TIGER grade line; it is a separately mapped grade, not the US 6 roadway, and does not ride any other railroad.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 6.7 mi against the documented 6.6 mi (Fowler: Newfield Junction 32.4 - Ulysses 39.0), 102%. 100% on ways tagged old_railway_operator=C&PA (three short pieces tagged railway=dismantled); no straight-line leg. The grade swings east of the direct line before turning north-west into Ulysses, so an extra shaping waypoint was placed on the grade at that bend (41.8855,-77.7455; not a station). Ulysses (borough) is 0.2 km from the line end. OSM also tags a further grade north of Ulysses and then east toward Genesee as C&PA; it is NOT drawn - the report's line ends at Ulysses (Fowler 39.0) and that grade's ownership is not established. LATER ALIGNMENT: none known; built standard gauge c.1895-97 and abandoned 1924.

segments.note: Newfield Junction - Perkins - Carpenter's - Crowell - Ulysses (Lewisville), connecting at Ulysses with the Fall Brook Railway (New York Central-leased from 1899). 1897 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start: Fowler letters z (1897 company timetable) at Perkins, Carpenter's, Crowells and Ulysses; WIKI says Ulysses was reached 'by 1895', and the 1896G at Newfield Junction does not prove Ulysses in 1896. 1919 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end, and it is the weakest date on this road: it rests on Fowler 'p' at Perkins and Crowell, and this road's legend gives p as '1919GG' - a code NOT defined in Fowler's Pennsylvania general legend, read here as a 1919 guide. The last year confirmed by a readable timetable is 1909 (CCP09, effective Aug 22 1909, still printed in Jan 1911); if 'GG' proves not to be a passenger guide, this segment's end falls back to 1909. Ulysses itself is not lettered p - only Crowell, about 3 mi short - so 1919 trains reaching Ulysses is an inference from the through timetables of 1901 and 1909. Upper bound: the line to Ulysses was abandoned in 1924 (WIKI, WIKIST) and Newfield Junction was the terminus by 1933 (Fowler c(tm)); 1924 is an abandonment ceiling, not a passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min is an estimate from the 2-3 trains each way a day Port Allegany - Ulysses in the 1901 and 1909 timetables (OCR, approximate), NOT a counted figure.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler (JF) section 385 letters z (1897), 1902G and p ('1919GG', undefined in the general legend); CCP01 and CCP09 timetables (1909 is the last year proven by a readable timetable); WIKI and WIKIST for the 1924 abandonment. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.
